doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Quitting school at sixteen to be a musician
summary: He left school at sixteen despite good grades; his father didn't speak to him for a long time and only conceded on his deathbed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was there a point in your life that you said I’m going to make a living as a musician?

That was when I was sixteen years old. What happened, I was doing very good in school, excellent you know, no problems. I was very good in mathematics. Mathematics has a lot to do with music, very closely associated. And I had two years to graduate. I turned sixteen, I went down and I quit school. My father didn’t talk to me for a long time after that. I quit school because I knew then what I wanted to do. I knew because I could tell by what I was playing and what I was hearing from people coming at me at the clubs I was playing, that it was there. I don’t know how but I knew it was there. So I stopped. Now on my father’s death bed, which was about six or seven years ago, he turned to me and he says, “Okay, you were right.” But it’s the truth. Because I wasn’t interested in college or this or that, I was interested in what I was doing musically. So that’s it. Period. That’s how it happened.
